title: Engineering non-ergodic properties in two dimensional quantum many-body systems
authors: Nyayabanta Swain, Gabriel Lemarié, Shaffique Adam
abstract: Non-ergodic quantum many-body dynamics offers a route to persistent quantum coherence far from equilibrium, beyond the conventional expectations of thermalizing statistical mechanics. Most known examples have been identified through intuition, analogy, or numerical search, rather than by systematic Hamiltonian design. This leaves few general methods for engineering robust non-ergodic dynamics in disorder-free interacting quantum many-body systems, especially in higher dimensions where enhanced connectivity generally disfavors ergodicity breaking. Here, we use an eigenstate-to-Hamiltonian construction approach to systematically engineer two-dimensional quantum spin Hamiltonians with tunable non-ergodic properties. Starting from a common parent model and input eigenstate, we construct two target Hamiltonians on the square lattice that differ in their interaction geometry: axial versus diagonal. We show that the resulting interaction geometry and coupling pattern control the Hilbert-space structure and dynamics. The axial model forms a connected Hilbert-space network and exhibits an anisotropy-driven crossover from ergodic to non-ergodic behavior through the suppression of resonances. In contrast, the diagonal model exhibits Hilbert-space fragmentation and, within its largest irreducible sector, signatures of quantum many-body scar dynamics including towers of highly localized, low-entanglement eigenstates, and long-lived coherent revivals. These results establish a direct link between Hamiltonian design, Hilbert-space network structure, and emergent non-ergodic dynamics.
summary: This paper introduces a systematic method, Eigenstate-to-Hamiltonian Construction (EHC), to engineer non-ergodic quantum dynamics in 2D spin systems. By constructing two Hamiltonians based on different interaction geometries (axial vs. diagonal), the authors show that the lattice structure directly controls the system's dynamics, leading to phenomena like Hilbert-space fragmentation and quantum scars.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of systematically engineering non-ergodic quantum dynamics in 2D interacting quantum many-body systems, moving beyond reliance on intuition or numerical search.
main_result: The authors successfully constructed two distinct 2D spin Hamiltonians ($	ilde{H}_{	ext{axial}}$ and $	ilde{H}_{	ext{diag}}$) using an eigenstate-to-Hamiltonian construction, demonstrating that the interaction geometry dictates the emergence of non-ergodic features like Hilbert-space fragmentation and quantum scars.
method: The core method is the Eigenstate-to-Hamiltonian Construction (EHC), which systematically builds target Hamiltonians whose eigenstates are known, circumventing the exponential scaling of the Hilbert space dimension.
model_or_system: The study focuses on spin-1/2 XXZ models on a square lattice in two dimensions. Two target Hamiltonians are constructed: one ($	ilde{H}_{	ext{axial}}$) using only nearest-neighbor (axial) couplings, and another ($	ilde{H}_{	ext{diag}}$) incorporating diagonal (next-nearest-neighbor) couplings.
key_observables: Hilbert-space fragmentation, quantum many-body scar signatures (low-entanglement, highly localized eigenstates), and the crossover between ergodic and non-ergodic dynamics.
important_parameters: Anisotropy ($\Delta$), interaction geometry (axial vs. diagonal), and the coupling strengths ($	ilde{J}^\perp_{b}, 	ilde{J}^{zz}_{b}$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the EHC method provides a systematic route to designing Hamiltonians with specific dynamical properties, particularly in 2D systems.
figures_summary: Figure 1 visually illustrates the construction process, showing the coupling patterns for the parent model and the two engineered target Hamiltonians ($	ilde{H}_{	ext{axial}}$ and $	ilde{H}_{	ext{diag}}$).
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem of engineering non-ergodicity, details the EHC methodology, applies it to construct two geometrically distinct 2D spin Hamiltonians, and then analyzes the resulting dynamics and Hilbert-space structure for both models.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, systematic theoretical tool (EHC) to design quantum models exhibiting specific non-equilibrium behaviors, which is highly relevant for understanding quantum simulation and controlling coherence in engineered quantum materials.

Study of the overlap of the ground state of parent Hamiltonian with all the eigenstates of the EHC built target Hamiltonians computed with exact diagonalization method. (a) For ˜Haxial, the overlap is negligible for most eigenstates except for a single eigenstate located in the middle of the spectrum for which the overlap approaches unity. This is independent of the value of ∆. (b) For ˜Hdiag, the overlap is negligible for almost all eigenstates except for few eigenstates located in the middle of the spec- trum. With increasing ∆, the maximum overlap approaches unity.
